standard.title: Impregnants for Power Capacitors — Specification (बिजली संधारित्रों (कैपेसिटरों) के लिए संसेचकों की विशिष्टि)

sectional_committee.name: Fluids for Electrotechnical Applications Sectional Committee

standard.description: This Indian Standard prescribes the quality baselines, physical-chemical characteristics, and testing methods for liquids used as impregnating agents in power capacitors conforming to IS 2834 : 1986.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard prescribes the quality baselines, physical-chemical characteristics, and testing methods for liquids used as impregnating agents in power capacitors conforming to IS 2834 : 1986.

version.current_version: First Edition, 1991 (Reaffirmed 2025) incorporating active Amendment No. 1
supersedes: None (Developed as a new standalone standard to govern quality specifications for modern paper and film power capacitor impregnants)

certification.description: Voluntary Product Specification. However, under public utility and industrial power factor correction (PFC) installation guidelines, power capacitors and their raw impregnants must carry test certificates verifying compliance with IS 13067 to ensure safety and grid stability.
requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, specific gravity decimals, or dissipation factors must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
Defined as the ratio of the weight in air of a given volume of the fluid at 29.5°C to the weight in air of an equal volume of water at 29.5°C.

Restricted to safe, non-toxic organic compounds, specifically covering Ester Compounds and Synthesised Hydrocarbon Compounds, while strictly excluding hazardous polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs/Askarels).

Determines the presence of acidic compounds by measuring the milligrams of KOH required to neutralize one gram of fluid. Acid limits are restricted to very low levels (typically <= 0.01 or 0.03 mg KOH/g) to prevent paper insulation breakdown.

Defined as the ratio of capacitance Cp of a given configuration of electrodes with the material as dielectric to capacitance Cv of the same electrode with air as dielectric, establishing standard dielectric spacing.
Evaluates specific insulation performance in ohm-centimeters (Ohm-cm), representing the ratio of potential gradient in volts/cm to current density in amperes/cm².
Measures the tangent of the angle (delta) by which the phase difference between applied voltage and resulting current deviates from pi/2 radian to control internal thermal dielectric losses.
